item.title: German chancellor arrives in Kyiv
item.content:encoded:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Ukraine on 4 October for a visit.

Source: German news agency dpa, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Merz's visit is intended to assure Ukraine of Germany's continued support in its fight against the Russian invasion.

Sources told dpa that this support will include interceptor drones and long-range weapons.

"If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us," Merz stated after arriving in Kyiv by train.

He is accompanied by Economy Minister Katherina Reiche and 10 heads of companies from the defence and energy sectors.

Government sources told dpa that Merz intends to make commitments to Ukraine regarding further financial and military support, including the delivery of thousands of interceptor drones and efforts to accelerate the production of long-range weapons.

Background:

  • Merz recently said he is working on solutions to strengthen Ukraine's air defence, which is currently Kyiv's biggest weakness.
  • On 29 September, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine had received air defence support packages from a number of countries.
  • European Pravda also reported, citing sources, on the possibility that one or several EU member states could transfer Patriot interceptors they already have to Ukraine, with Ukraine using funds from the €90 billion loan to order an equivalent number of missiles for that state from the US manufacturer.

item.title: Russian drones attack Kyiv: debris falls on roof of house in Dniprovskyi district
item.content:encoded:
Russian drones attacked Kyiv repeatedly overnight and on the morning of 4 October, causing a fire at a non-residential building in the Desnianskyi district. Debris also fell onto the roof of a house in the Dniprovskyi district.

Source: Kyiv City Military Administration; Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko

Quote from Klitschko: "In the Dniprovskyi district, UAV debris fell onto the roof of a house. There was no fire. Debris also fell in an open area near a road in the same district. There was no fire there either."

Details: An air-raid warning was issued six times in the capital overnight and in the morning due to the drone threat.

During one of the attacks, falling debris caused a fire at a non-residential building in the Desnianskyi district.

item.title: Russia loses 1,750 soldiers over past day
item.content:encoded:
Russia has lost 1,750 soldiers killed and wounded over the past day, bringing its total number of personnel losses to 1,540,700.

Source: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on Facebook

Details: The total combat losses of the Russian forces between 24 February 2022 and 4 October 2026 are estimated to be as follows [figures in parentheses represent the latest losses – ed.]:

  • approximately 1,540,700 (+1,760) military personnel
  • 12,391 (+0) tanks
  • 25,483 (+6) armoured combat vehicles
  • 50,686 (+49) artillery systems
  • 2,179 (+1) multiple-launch rocket systems
  • 1,686 (+3) air defence systems
  • 443 (0) fixed-wing aircraft
  • 356 (+0) helicopters
  • 2,837 (+13) ground robotic systems
  • 546,240 (+1,742) operational-tactical UAVs
  • 5,126 (+0) cruise missiles
  • 35 (+0) ships/boats
  • 2 (+0) submarines
  • 157,258 (+527) vehicles and fuel tankers
  • 4,788 (+5) special vehicles and other equipment

The information is being confirmed.

item.title: Russian forces attack Dnipropetrovsk Oblast over 40 times: three injured
item.content:encoded:
Three people were injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on 3 October.

Source: Oleksandr Hanzha, Head of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration

Quote: "Three people have been injured. The enemy has attacked three districts more than 40 times using drones, artillery and an aerial bomb."

Details: Russian forces struck food warehouses in Pavlohrad, causing a fire. Two people were injured.

The city of Nikopol and the Marhanets, Chervonohryhorivka and Pokrovske hromadas came under attack in the Nikopol district. Infrastructure, an apartment building, shops, a hardware store, an outbuilding and a car were damaged.

A 34-year-old man was injured. He is receiving outpatient treatment.

In the Synelnykove district, the Russians struck the Malomykhailivka hromada.

item.title: Up to 140 sq km already liberated in Operation Vivaldi, Zelenskyy says
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stated that 125-140 sq km of territory has been liberated in the course of the Operation Vivaldi counteroffensive so far, and there has been a significant increase in Russian casualties over the past two to three months.

Source: Zelenskyy in an interview with Reuters, excerpts from which he posted on social media

Quote from Zelenskyy: "Vivaldi is a very successful operation. It's not finished yet. As of today, about 125-140 square kilometres have been de-occupied."

Details: Zelenskyy said the number of Russians killed and wounded has increased over the last two to three months.

Quote: "Since the beginning of the year, they had 30,000-32,000 casualties per month – 21,000-22,000 killed and others badly wounded. Now, we are talking about 42,000 casualties a month. So, during the offensive, we lost several times fewer people than Russia, and they have been on the defensive."

Details: He noted that the Ukrainian military wanted to launch Operation Vivaldi a year ago, but more preparations were needed.

Quote: "Thank God, we decided to postpone it a bit, and now we have good results and fewer losses."

Background:

  • On 15 September, the Third Army Corps reported that 75 sq km of territory had been mopped up and another 10 sq km liberated as part of counteroffensive actions in the northern part of Donetsk Oblast.
  • On 20 September, it was reported that as part of Operation Vivaldi, the Third Army Corps had liberated the villages of Shandryholove and Derylove in Donetsk Oblast and established full control over Drobysheve.
  • On 28 September, Brigadier General Andrii Biletskyi, commander of the Third Army Corps, reported that the Russians had lost 2,000 personnel during the third phase of Operation Vivaldi and over 250 Russian soldiers were taken prisoner.

item.title: Zelenskyy: US must not forget it is a hundred times stronger than Russia in negotiations
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said the US must not forget how strong it is in negotiations with Russia, noting that Vladimir Putin has begun to think that he is the one who gets to make decisions.

Source: Zelenskyy in an interview with Reuters, an excerpt from which he posted on social media, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Zelenskyy said he believes the US genuinely wants to end Russia's war.

Quote from Zelenskyy: "I think the US really wants to stop Russia's war. I trust them. Then, I understand it's difficult to stop somebody who's big and doesn't want to stop. That's why you're trying to find some compromises with Russia. But I think we are losing time if we want to play with Russian compromises."

Details: Zelenskyy emphasised that President Donald Trump now wants to achieve some kind of victory before the midterm elections, but, he said, Putin will do all he can to encourage the Iranians and make negotiations impossible.

Quote: "President Trump wants to have some kind of victory before the midterms. But Putin will do everything to push the Iranians and make this whole situation non-negotiable.

The same with Russia's war against Ukraine. If Putin sees that President Trump needs some victory, he will decide what to give and what not to give. And this is the problem – Putin has started to think that it is he who can decide. But America is one hundred times stronger than Russia. Absolutely. They just have to remember that."

Background:

  • The New York Times previously reported that the White House is considering signing certain business deals with Russia as a way of demonstrating its good intentions.
  • According to the NYT, the US and Russia are also negotiating a multi-billion-dollar deal regarding Lukoil's vast global portfolio of oil fields, refineries and petrol stations. Lukoil is one of Russia's largest energy companies.
  • Separately, The Atlantic reported that Trump has agreed to a proposal from his special envoy John Coale to ease sanctions against Russia in exchange for the release of some prisoners held in Russia.

item.title: Zelenskyy: FP-9 ballistic missile capable of reaching Moscow will be ready this autumn
item.content:encoded:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stated that Ukraine's FP-9 ballistic missile, which is capable of reaching Moscow, will be ready this autumn.

Source: Zelenskyy in an interview with Reuters

Details: Reuters noted that Ukraine reported the first combat deployment of its domestically produced FP-7 ballistic missile this week. The missile has a range of approximately 250 km.

Zelenskyy said he had phoned the manufacturer, Fire Point, to urge them to speed up development of the longer-range FP-9 model, which the company says will be able to strike Moscow.

Quote from Zelenskyy: "I said to them, where is my FP-9? [with a grin – ed.] We need the FP-9. And the FP-9 will be [ready] this autumn, I'm sure."

Details: Zelenskyy also pointed out that Ukraine has had to rely heavily on its F-16 and MiG fighter jets to shoot down about 60% of Russian jet-powered UAVs, but stocks of 20mm ammunition for these aircraft are running extremely low.

He said Kyiv is urgently seeking alternative solutions, particularly by enhancing its electronic warfare capabilities. The first delivery of small, inexpensive air defence missiles capable of shooting down the new Shaheds is expected in the second half of October.

Last week Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine is developing five new interceptor models designed to down jet-powered Shaheds. Having just returned from a meeting with the leadership of the Ministry of Defence, he mentioned that the testing of two of these models had demonstrated a moderate success rate of around 30%.

Quote: "We'll have to scale it. I hope that with all these things, with all these elements, we'll find a way."

item.title: Ukraine will step up strikes on Russian refineries in response to Moscow's aerial terror, Zelenskyy says
item.content:encoded:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Ukraine will increase its strikes on Russian oil refineries in response to Moscow's new campaign of airstrikes aimed at forcing people to flee Kyiv and other cities.

Source: Zelenskyy in an interview with Reuters

Details: Zelenskyy said Ukraine will react to Moscow's change of tactics, but it will not respond in kind by indiscriminately striking civilian infrastructure.

Quote from Zelenskyy: "We have to respond in any way [we can]. With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners: what gives money to them for this war. But we will not respond, of course, just like them, on any civilian objects."

Details: Zelenskyy also noted that Ukrainian intelligence has obtained documents indicating that Russian leader Vladimir Putin has issued a "new doctrine" of military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter.

Quote: "We saw documents and we know that they allow them to attack infrastructure ... logistics ... roads, schools, hospitals, to pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities. This is the goal of the operation."

Details: According to Zelenskyy, the reason for the policy shift was Putin's desire to appear strong at a time when his troops are losing ground in Donbas and suffering heavy casualties.

item.title: Chișinău summons Russian ambassador over entry of missiles and drones into Moldova
item.content:encoded:
Moldova's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has summoned Russian Ambassador Oleg Ozerov to deliver a protest note regarding the unauthorised entry into Moldovan airspace of five drones and missiles, which exploded near populated areas in four districts.

Source: Moldova's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Saturday 3 October; European Pravda

Details: The Moldovan Foreign Ministry stressed the seriousness of the incident, which put people's lives and safety at risk and caused fires and damage. Ozerov was summoned to the Foreign Ministry over the incident.

The ministry urged Russia to respect Moldova's sovereignty and territorial integrity and ensure that similar incidents do not happen again.

Background:

  • On 3 October, Moldova's national airspace monitoring system recorded the entry of several unmanned aerial vehicles. The National Army's Air Operations Service reported that five UAVs had crossed Moldovan airspace between 07:45 and 08:00.
  • Defence Minister Anatolie Nosatîi later clarified that the incident involved three missiles and two drones, debris from which fell in four different districts.
  • The Moldovan Defence Ministry subsequently reported a sixth unauthorised entry into its airspace amid Russia's massive morning attack on Ukraine.
  • Ozerov was also summoned to the Moldovan Foreign Ministry over drone incidents on 1 October.

item.title: Drone crashes on road in Kirovohrad Oblast: man killed, woman injured
item.content:encoded:
A man has been killed and a woman injured as a result of a UAV crash-landing on a road in the town of Haivoron in Kirovohrad Oblast on Saturday.

Source: Andrii Raikovych, Head of Kirovohrad Oblast Military Administration

Quote from Raikovych: "A man has been killed as a result of a UAV crashing on a road in the town of Haivoron during an air raid. A woman was also injured. She has been taken to hospital."

Details: Dry grass caught fire at the site where the drone debris fell. The fire has been contained.

item.title: Ukraine has hit targets in Russia's Samara and Bryansk oblasts, Zelenskyy says – video
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Ukraine has struck targets in Russia's Samara Oblast and the positions of Russian forces operating Iskander missile systems in Bryansk Oblast over the past 24 hours. He also reported "new results" in the Black Sea.

Source: Zelenskyy on social media

Quote from Zelenskyy: "Over the past 24 hours, our long-range capabilities effectively struck targets serving the aggressor's war machine. Our sanctions reached the Samara region, as well as the positions of occupiers operating Iskander missile systems in the Bryansk region. There are new results in the Black Sea."

https://www.facebook.com/reel/1074616938516319

Details: Zelenskyy also reported that a Russian Shahed drone struck the Pivnichnyi (North) Bridge in Kyiv in the morning. Russian forces attacked residential buildings and rail and energy infrastructure in several regions. In Chornomorsk, a drone hit a vessel.

Quote from Zelenskyy: "Importantly, our warriors always find a way to justly respond to these attacks and take the war back to where it came from."

item.title: Disabled Ukrainian woman abducted by Russians from Oleshky care home goes missing in Russia
item.content:encoded:
Relatives and acquaintances have lost contact with Anastasiia Mamotiuk, a Ukrainian citizen who was abducted by Russian forces from the Oleshky psychoneurological care home and taken to Russia.

Source: Emile Foundation, a humanitarian organisation

Details: Emile Foundation told Ukrainska Pravda.Zhyttia (Life) that contact with Mamotiuk was lost while arrangements were being made for her return to Ukraine.

The Russians occupied the Oleshky care home in Kherson Oblast in the very first days of the full-scale invasion and began deporting its residents in 2022. In November 2023, Anastasiia was among three adults taken to Penza, Russia.

Oleksandr Danylchuk, one of the residents who subsequently returned to Ukraine, said they were told about the relocation just one day before leaving. They were not asked whether they wanted to go to Russia.

Anastasiia and the others were moved to Novye Berega (New Shores), an assisted living facility for people with disabilities run by Sofia Lvova-Belova, the sister of Maria Lvova-Belova, Russia's Presidential Commissioner for Children's Rights.

Danylchuk said he told Sofia Lvova-Belova that he wanted to return to his friends and family in Ukraine, but Russian officials publicly claimed that the abducted Ukrainians did not want to go home.

Despite being illegally taken to Russia, Anastasiia remained in contact with people in Ukraine: Viacheslav Shchyrskyi, her foster father in the House of Stefan family, whom she regarded as her own family; a former teacher at the care home; and Oleksandr Danylchuk.

Shchyrskyi had previously sought the organisation's help in securing Anastasiia's return to Ukraine. He is close to her and plans to become her legal guardian. Together with the foundation, he prepared and submitted official appeals to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukrainian Parliamentary Commissioner for Human Rights, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), and Russia's commissioner for human rights.

The Emile Foundation says Anastasiia repeatedly said she wanted to return to Ukraine and that she feared for her own safety in Russia. She cannot yet leave the country because she is waiting for the passport she needs to travel, the foundation said.

Maria Lvova-Belova released a video of the young woman on 16 September. According to the organisation, the video provides no way to assess the Ukrainian woman's health or the circumstances in which it was recorded and cannot replace direct, confidential communication with her.

Over the last few days, direct contact with her has been lost. As of 1 October, three former residents of the Oleshky care home – Anastasiia Mamotiuk, Viktoriia Markeliuk and Anastasiia Yavorska – are still in Penza, the Emile Foundation has learned.

The foundation is calling for an immediate, independent assessment of Anastasiia's safety and health, the confidentiality of communication to be ensured, direct contact to be restored, and international support to be provided for her return.

Mariam Lambert, CEO and co-founder of the Emile Foundation, says Nastia must never be used as a pawn in political bargaining. She says Nastia is a woman with a disability who has the right to safety, dignity and the freedom to make decisions about her own life.

Lambert says that, for the first time, none of those helping Nastia return to Ukraine have been able to contact her. She says an independent assessment of Nastia's condition and safety, the restoration of communication, and concrete diplomatic action to ensure her safe return to Ukraine are urgently needed.

At the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, 101 people were living at the Oleshky care home, including children and adults with various forms of disability. Most were not orphans or children deprived of parental care.

In October 2022, the Russian military began moving the residents to different institutions. In total, Russia abducted 84 people, 13 of whom their families managed to bring back.

One of the care home's residents was taken away and ended up with a Russian family – a Russian soldier who had fought against Ukraine tried to adopt her.

The foundation said that the lack of a legal mechanism for the return of adults with disabilities is one of the main obstacles to bringing them back.

According to Lambert, a permanent international humanitarian mechanism should be established to facilitate the return of adults, with the involvement of intermediary countries.

Previously: Two Russian-installed Donetsk officials are suspected of deporting 31 Ukrainian children to Russia for "medical treatment".

Lvova-Belova said a Ukrainian teenager abducted from Mariupol and "adopted" by her would become a prosecutor.

item.title: Kyiv authorities retract report of drone debris falling on apartment block
item.content:encoded:
Kyiv authorities initially said debris from a Russian drone had fallen on the roof of a multi-storey building in Kyiv's Obolonskyi district and caused a fire, but later withdrew the report, saying it had not been confirmed.

Source: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko; Kyiv City Military Administration

Quote from Klitschko: "A fire has broken out on the roof of a multi-storey building in the Obolonskyi district as a result of the fall of debris. Early reports indicate there is no destruction and no casualties. Emergency services are heading to the scene."

Details: Kyiv City Military Administration explained that the fire had broken out on the roof of a 16-storey residential building in the Obolonskyi district due to the fall of debris.

An air-raid warning was in effect in Kyiv from 17:32 to 17:53 due to the threat of Russian UAVs.

Update: At 18:26, Kyiv City Military Administration said that reports of drone debris falling and a fire in the Obolonskyi district had not been confirmed.

This news has been updated since publication.

item.title: Ukraine to set up working group to identify fallen soldiers
item.content:encoded:
Ukraine's National Security and Defence Council will establish a working body to consider issues related to the identification of fallen military personnel.

Source: Ihor Klymenko, Secretary of the National Security and Defence Council (NSDC), on Telegram

Quote: "For families of missing people, having to wait a long time to learn what happened to their loved ones only adds to their pain. The state must do everything it can to speed up the process and ensure that examinations are carried out properly."

Details: Klymenko said that, on President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's instructions, Ukraine plans to strengthen its forensic examination system. The number of experts will be increased, and steps will be taken to improve working conditions.

In addition, specialised regional bureaus will be set up to focus solely on identifying the remains of military personnel.

Quote: "From now on, this work will be overseen by the National Security and Defence Council. The relevant working group will bring together all the state institutions involved. We need to look at the entire process as a whole: where delays occur, what decisions are still needed and who is responsible for implementing them. Families do not need explanations for why the system is slow, they need answers."

Background:

  • On 2 October, a meeting of the Coordination Council on the Protection of the Rights of War Veterans and Their Family Members, Family Members of Fallen Defenders of Ukraine, Prisoners of War and Missing Persons, was held at the Office of the President.
  • Following the meeting, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said the Cabinet of Ministers will adopt all the necessary regulations by mid- October to help forensic groups work faster and more effectively. "Another important issue is the approval of international agreements that will help strengthen efforts to find missing Ukrainian defenders and identify them. Our international partners are willing to actively support us in this, and we should make use of this opportunity," the prime minister added.
  • Kyrylo Budanov, Head of the President's Office, previously said a significant number of the 26,000 bodies and remains brought back from Russia have yet to be identified.
  • He added that Ukraine would establish an interagency group to address issues related to the identification of the fallen. The work of forensic examination bureaus is also planned to be reviewed, and "international capabilities" will be involved in identifying the dead.

item.title: Kyiv is preparing pontoon crossings in case of bridge strikes and planning tunnel under Dnipro River – minister
item.content:encoded:
The construction of several reserve pontoon crossings across the Dnipro River is scheduled to begin in Kyiv next week, and a long-term option of building a tunnel under the river is also being considered.

Source: Mykola Kalashnyk, Ukraine's Minister of Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport, in an interview with Suspilne

Details: Kalashnyk said a quick option for connecting the left and right banks of Kyiv in the event of bridge damage is currently being considered: building earth dams with pontoon crossings to maintain traffic across the Dnipro River.

Quote from Kalashnyk: "Urgent solutions include a dam and a pontoon crossing, which can be built quickly... This work has already begun. A corresponding coordination meeting was held by the president. We have received all the tasks taking into account their critical nature. The city did not deal with this on its own, so the decision was made for the ministry, the Agency for Restoration, and the military to tackle this together with the capital's authorities."

Details: The minister noted that the construction of the crossings could take up to three months, and the structures themselves should provide at least half the capacity of the existing bridges.

Quote from Kalashnyk: "Preparatory work is underway, and construction will begin shortly. All infrastructure will be involved to maximise the percentage of throughput. We have an average of about 600,000 cars crossing between the left and right banks per day. And the task is to preserve this capacity."

Details: The minister said the locations where construction will begin have been determined. The work is planned not only in Kyiv but also in other regions of Ukraine, and not just on the Dnipro River.

Furthermore, the ministry is considering other options, including the construction of quick-assembly concrete structures and, in the long term, a tunnel under the Dnipro River. However, such projects could cost tens of billions of hryvnias, so their implementation is only possible with the support of Kyiv's international partners.

Meanwhile, the main priority remains preserving the bridges and preventing their destruction. "The maximum amount of equipment has been deployed" for this purpose, the minister added.

Quote from Kalashnyk: "Obviously, each [bridge – ed.] has a margin of safety. And our first task is to provide protection from the sky, which we are doing in coordination with the military. So the first step is to prevent strikes. The second part is to provide protection. The third is rapid recovery. And the fourth is to make decisions regarding alternative reserve crossings, i.e., the construction of new alternative bridge infrastructure facilities."

item.title: Moldova reports sixth unauthorised flight in airspace amid Russian attack on Ukraine
item.content:encoded:
Moldova's Ministry of Defence reported a sixth unauthorised flight in the country's airspace on Saturday amid a massive morning Russian attack on Ukraine.

Source: Moldova's Ministry of Defence on Facebook; European Pravda

Details: The ministry reported that the drone had been detected during an analysis of airspace data.

According to the Defence Ministry, the object entered Moldovan airspace at 08:04 from the village of Udobne in Ukraine's Odesa Oblast, heading towards the Moldovan village of Palanca.

At 08:05, the object left Moldovan territory and moved towards the Ukrainian town of Biliaivka.

The Moldovan National Army's radars have recorded a total of six unauthorised flights over the country.

Background:

  • On 3 October, Moldova's national airspace monitoring system recorded the flight of several unmanned aerial vehicles. The National Army's Air Operations Service reported that five unmanned aerial vehicles had crossed the national airspace between 07:45 and 08:00.
  • Defence Minister Anatolie Nosatîi later clarified that the incident involved three missiles and two drones, the wreckage of which fell in four districts in the country.
  • Moldovan President Maia Sandu reacted by stating that the Russian war is "dangerously close to Moldova".

item.title: Russian-to-Ukrainian force ratio is 6:1 in some areas – Ukrainian National Guard commander
item.content:encoded:
Oleksandr Pivnenko, Commander of Ukraine's National Guard, has again said that Russian forces outnumber Ukrainian troops by six to one in some frontline areas in Donetsk Oblast.

Source: Pivnenko on Facebook

Details: Pivnenko reported that he had recently visited National Guard units performing combat missions in Kharkiv and Donetsk oblasts.

Quote from Pivnenko: "The situation on these fronts remains dynamic. Over the past week alone, our units have repelled more than 170 enemy attacks in their areas of responsibility.

The highest number of assaults occurred in Donetsk Oblast, where in some areas the ratio of advancing enemy forces to ours is 6 to 1."

Details: Pivnenko noted that Russian troops continue to actively use infantry, drones and aircraft. Despite this, Ukrainian soldiers are holding their positions, thwarting Russian assaults and inflicting personnel and equipment losses on the Russians.

Ukrainian units can strike targets 70-100 km behind Russian lines using mid-range capabilities, the National Guard Commander noted.

Background: In July, Pivnenko also reported a six-to-one ratio of Russian to Ukrainian forces in some frontline areas.

item.title: Donnyland abandoned: the last negotiations of the year
Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges could create "logistical nightmare" for Ukraine, NYT reports
item.content:encoded:
Russian attacks could force the Ukrainian authorities to close Kyiv's bridges for an extended period, resulting in a "logistical nightmare" for the capital and the whole of Ukraine.

Source: The New York Times

Details: Kyiv's bridges are essential for transporting food and equipment across the Dnipro River. If the crossings are closed, there will be few alternative routes, and transportation will require long detours, the NYT notes.

The NYT reports that the nearest road bridge south of Kyiv is about 145 km away, a drive of roughly two and a half hours. Other crossings further downstream are closer to the front, making them even more vulnerable to Russian attacks.

The newspaper estimates that Russian forces have attacked the capital's bridges six times between 1 and 3 October: five strikes hit the Pivdennyi (South) Bridge, and one hit the Pivnichnyi (North) Bridge. The damage and the threat of repeat attacks have led to traffic restrictions or a complete halt on five of the city's six road bridges.

The bridges are still standing, but further strikes could weaken their supporting structures. The authorities could then close the crossings indefinitely to reduce the risk of collapse, the NYT explains.

The daily commute for many Kyiv residents is also at risk. About a million people live on the predominantly residential left bank, while most government institutions and businesses are concentrated on the right bank.

Ukrainian officials and military experts cited by the NYT believe the strikes on the bridges are part of a campaign to destroy Ukraine's economy and undermine its ability to sustain the war effort. Russian forces are also attacking warehouses, railways, data centres, medical facilities and steel plants.

Background:

  • On 1 October, two drones struck near the supporting structure of the Pivdennyi (South) Bridge. Following the strikes, metro and overground public transport services across the crossing were suspended so that the structures could be inspected.
  • On 2 October, Kyiv City Military Administration reported that damage had been caused to a support, the road surface and the concrete protection of the metro tracks following previous attacks.
  • The Kyiv Metro is prepared to resume services across the Pivdennyi Bridge during "yellow" alerts (warnings issued in response to drone threats), but only after receiving an expert assessment of the bridge's condition.
  • On 2 October, another strike on the Pivdennyi Bridge was recorded in Kyiv.
  • On 3 October, a Russian jet-powered drone struck Kyiv's Pivnichnyi (North) Bridge, which connects the right and left banks of the Dnipro River.

item.title: Ukraine receives €50m from Council of Europe bank and Italy for destroyed housing compensation
item.content:encoded:
Ukraine has received €50 million under the Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB) project HOME: Compensation for Destroyed Housing. The funds will be used to finance housing certificates under the state-run eRecovery programme.

Source: Ukraine's Ministry of Finance; European Pravda

Details: CEB provided €25 million, and another €25 million was contributed with financial support from the Italian government.

The framework agreement on the second additional financing for the HOME project was signed on 26 June during the Ukraine Recovery Conference (URC-2026) in Gdańsk.

The total volume of the new financing package is €100 million, half of which – €50 million – is being provided by the Italian government through the CEB mechanism.

Ukraine previously raised €200 million under the earlier stages of the HOME project. These funds financed over 6,000 housing certificates for citizens who lost their homes as a result of the war.

Background:

  • At the end of September, the international Register of Damage caused by Russian aggression against Ukraine opened all 43 categories envisaged by its mandate for the submission of claims. This marked the completion of the phased launch of the claims submission system, which began in April 2024.
